title: kvu: a generator and measurement bench for lattice gauge theory (SU(2) Wilson action, single-source HIP/CUDA kernels, FP64 CPU reference)
description:
kvu is a Rust command-line tool for lattice gauge theory, centred on four-dimensional SU(2) Yang-Mills theory with the Wilson action. One GPU kernel source serves two backends, HIP (AMD) and CUDA (NVIDIA), compiled at run time, next to a double-precision CPU reference. Every run writes a provenance manifest (binary hash, commit, source fingerprint, seeds, options), and configurations can be archived, verified and regenerated bit for bit.

Contents: a heat-bath and overrelaxation generator with counter-based Philox4x32-10 random numbers (FP64 reference, whose GPU outputs with the compat-prod options are bit-identical to those of the published generator su2-heatbath-gpu, and a fast FP32 mode); Dirichlet boxes; a conditional heat bath; Wilson and Polyakov loops, gradient flow and topological charge; Balaban (L_b = 3) and Swendsen (b = 2) block-spin maps and effective-coupling estimators; the Hessian of the Wilson action on a given background; a group registry with known-answer gates (SU(2), Sp(4)). Four modules added in November 2026 are instruments: verifiable compressed archives (kvu-archive/1), couplings of a truncated effective action (plaquette, rectangle, chair, twist) by pseudo-likelihood and Schwinger-Dyson equations with jackknife errors, block-face flux statistics, and 't Hooft twisted boundary conditions (CPU FP64).

It is a tool, not a physics result: it contains and claims no result on the mass gap, the continuum limit or any new constant. The test suite (cargo test) checks known answers, independent Python references, bit-identity and deliberate mutants; GPU tests are opt-in. Documentation is in French.

The code and documentation were written by AI coding agents under the direction of the author; see AI_USE.md.
notes: Tested on Linux x86_64 with an AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, ROCm 7.1) and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (sm_120, CUDA 13). See README.md (contents, installation, minimal examples, known limitations), CHANGELOG.md and AI_USE.md.
